run.request: I have a job offer for $96,000 as a senior operations analyst. I want $110,000. The offer expires in three days. How do I ask for more without losing the offer, and what do I say on the call?
run.title: Ask for $110,000 without losing the offer
run.goal: Plan and make one call that asks for more pay and keeps the offer safe.
run.summary: Book a call on day 1 and ask once for $110,000 with two proof points. Counters rarely cost offers, so never accept on the call and confirm in writing.

sections.heading: Is the ask safe

body.text: A polite counter rarely costs you an offer, and employers expect one. $110,000 is about 15% above $96,000, which is a normal ask for a senior role.

items: Search your exact title plus your city on each site below.
Write down the low, middle and high figure from each.
Use base salary only. Leave out bonus and stock.
Match the seniority. Skip junior and manager listings.
If $110,000 is at or below the high end, the ask is fair.

body.text: BLS has no category for senior operations analysts. Use its operations research analyst figure as a rough guide only.

items: Above the middle of the range: give two or three strong reasons.
Above the high end: expect a partial raise, not the full amount.
Big-city or tech-company pay usually runs 10% to 20% higher.

body.text: Together the sources give an estimated base range of $85,000 to $130,000. $110,000 sits inside it.

revised: Change "almost never costs you an offer" to "rarely costs you an offer". The current wording promises too much.
Label BLS operations research analysts as the closest match, not your exact role.
Make the handoff range match the table ($85k to $130k), or say why $90k to $120k was used.

body.text: On day 1, send a short email to book a 15-minute call for day 2. Sample: "Thank you for the offer. I'm excited about the role and would like a 15-minute call tomorrow to talk about pay."
Also on day 1, write your proof points on one page. Keep the page in front of you on the call.

items: Results with numbers, like costs cut or hours saved
Tools the role needs that you already use, like SQL or Excel
The market pay range from the research above
One goal from the job post you can help with right away

rows: Write three or four proof points

body.text: Say these lines in order. Fill in the brackets with your own proof points first.

items: "Thank you for the offer. I'm excited about this role."
"I want to join the team, and I'd like to make this work."
"Given the role's scope, I'm asking for a base salary of $110,000."
"In my last role, I cut [process] time by [X percent]."
"I can own [key duty from the job post] from day one."
Then stop talking. Let the silence sit until they answer.
Say $110,000 once, clearly. Don't add "or so" or "if possible."
Never say yes on the call. Thank them and confirm in writing.
If they say "that's our max," switch to the trades below.

sections.heading: If base won't move

items: Ask for one or two trades, not the whole list at once.
Lead with a signing bonus. It closes the first-year gap fastest.
Ask that the 6-month review set a target of $104,000 to $110,000.
If cash is truly capped, pick the perk you value most.
Ask them to put every agreed change in a revised offer letter.

body.text: Accept only after the revised letter lists every change you agreed on. Reply in writing before the day 3 deadline.

rows: Covers part or all of first-year gap
Saves about $1,000 to $3,000 a year in commute costs
Builds skills for your next raise

revised: Cut "even if you said yes on the call." The call script says never say yes on the call.
Signing bonus row: change "Covers the $14,000 gap" to "Covers part or all of first-year gap".
Give remote days a dollar estimate, like $1,000 to $3,000 a year in commute savings.

next_steps: Check $110,000 against the four pay sources today.
Email to book a 15-minute call for day 2.
Write your one-page list of proof points.
Make the call and ask for $110,000 once.
Send your written answer by noon on day 3.
assumptions: US-based full-time role with a written offer in hand
You have no competing offer right now
Base salary matters most, but perks also count
You can schedule a call within two days
All pay figures are estimates and vary by city
checks: Script asks for exactly $110,000 and gives clear reasons
Plan fits inside the three-day deadline, with the reply sent early
Includes replies for "no", "maybe" and "let me check" answers
Lists at least three non-salary trades with estimated dollar values
Says to get any new terms in writing before accepting
conflicts: call-script says never say yes on the call. if-they-say-no says "even if you said yes on the call."
if-they-say-no sets the 6-month review target at $105,000 in the list but $104,000 to $110,000 in the table.
risk-and-number handoff gives the market range as $90,000 to $120,000, but its table runs from $85,000 to $130,000.
